scope: Read-only repository/source and exact stock ELF review. No SSH, device writes, reboot, Git staging, or commit was performed by this reviewer.

authorization.permanent_boot_slot_commit: Pending clarification by root agent; this report does not grant authorization.

core_findings: The new-layout eMMC metadata has one COMMITTED integer (0, 1, or 2). The bcm_bootstate per-slot commit flags are equality tests against that singleton, not two independent flags.

Thus slot1 permanently selected plus slot2 commit flag 1 is impossible with this stock metadata format. Permanent slot1 selection changes slot2 displayed commit flag to 0, while retaining VALID=1,2 and the original slot2 payload.
After an accepted slot1 trial with the one-time request already consumed, bcm_bootstate +1 alone sets the persistent default to slot1. bcm_bootstate 5 is not an additional required operation.
Never use bcm_bootstate -1 to restore stock default: it can set COMMITTED=0 and cause the bootloader to select the newer slot1 by sequence. Use +2 to restore COMMITTED=2.

commit() can invoke reboot when /var/gpt_modified.txt exists and /proc/cmdline contains gpt. Require the marker to be absent before either +1 or rollback +2; do not remove an unexplained marker automatically.

The metadata writer writes both copies but does not propagate each setEmmcMetadata return through wr_metadata. Exit status alone cannot establish durable success; verify both physical copies independently.

The early read-only guard can be deliberately relaxed with BLKROSET (blockdev --setrw) and reapplied with blockdev --setro. It does not protect whole-disk raw writes, so no raw whole-disk operation is in this plan.

static_evidence_detail.finding: Read flag returns ASCII 1 iff requested partition equals metadata committed; +1 stores partition into committed and valid[partition-1], then writes metadata.
Serializes COMMITTED, VALID and SEQ, computes CRC, calls metadata writes for copies1 and2; setEmmcMetadata uses fflush/fsync/fclose. Caller ignores per-copy failure.
After metadata write, /var/gpt_modified.txt stat plus successful grep -q gpt /proc/cmdline can call logged reboot.
New-layout next boot state follows committed slot and getBootReason. Setting permanent slot1 only commits it if needed. A consumed trial has no activation pending.

With both images valid, committed chooses default; activation/fallback flags may select 3-committed. Failed-image fallback depends on compiled bootloader support and is not guaranteed by existence of another valid payload.
CRC covers bytes at offset12 for (second LE uint32 minus4)&0xffff bytes; parses singleton COMMITTED plus VALID and SEQ.
Only metadata GPT partitions1/2 marked RO during partition registration; BLKROSET intentionally supported.

bounded_sequence_after_authorization: Use one root shell with a unique commit lock and EXIT/HUP/INT/TERM handling that syncs and restores BOTH metadata partitions to RO on every exit. Keep all checks and backups before unlock.
blockdev --setrw /dev/mmcblk0p1; blockdev --setrw /dev/mmcblk0p2. Verify each /sys/class/block/mmcblk0pN/ro reads0. If any unlock/check fails, restore BOTH to RO and stop.
/bin/bcm_bootstate +1, capture full output and exit code; sync. Do not call5 redundantly and do not reboot.
Immediately restore blockdev --setro on BOTH metadata partitions and confirm each ro file reads1, including if +1 reports failure.
Read bcm_bootstate and read both physical metadata partitions independently. Validate CRC and exact COMMITTED=1, VALID=1,2, SEQ=5,4 in both copies. Verify all expected CLI labels below and no ONCE.
Recheck original slot2 full hashes, same boot_id, kernel9 uname/root, and metadata RO1/1. Save hashes/raw metadata locally as private evidence.
Only mark permanent commit accepted if all readbacks pass. This sequence proves metadata selection without reboot; a later reboot acceptance is a separate observed result.

expected_fallback_integrity.recovery_note: Original slot2 remains selectable recovery firmware; permanent slot1 default removes the current unconditional next-reset-to-stock behavior.

failure_recovery: On any ambiguous write/readback outcome, preserve live kernel9 session and do not reboot or claim successful commit.

If metadata remains readable and marker remains absent, perform bounded rollback to the saved default using the same guarded RW window: bcm_bootstate +2; sync; restore BOTH metadata partitions RO; verify BOTH copies CRC plus COMMITTED=2, VALID=1,2, SEQ=5,4 and Reboot Partition: Second.
Do not use -1 as a fallback reset, do not clear VALID entries, do not touch slot2 payloads, and do not issue5/7 blindly.

If +2 cannot restore both metadata copies, stop further automatic mutations and keep the current session alive. The verified full metadata backups are available for an explicitly reviewed recovery; this plan does not claim rollback is guaranteed under storage failure.
